_readme: CAGE for the EXTERNAL (untrusted, e.g. GLM) worker seat. Rendered into
spawn time — the agent never authors it and cannot edit it (see .claude deny).
{{WORKTREE}} is substituted with the absolute worktree path. The '//' prefix
is FILESYSTEM-ABSOLUTE. A single leading '/' would anchor to THIS FILE's
directory, not the fs root — that is the anchoring trap; never write '/foo'.
What these rules do and do NOT do (proved empirically, decisions.md D-11):
DO   block Claude's own Edit/Write tools on the Critical Files (threat T1).
DO NOT stop a secret read: `python3 -c "print(open('.env').read())"` walks
straight through Read(...) deny, because deny only covers the built-in
file tools plus RECOGNIZED bash commands (cat/head/tail/sed). Secrets
are contained by W1 (dummy .env in the worktree) + the OS sandbox.
The Read/Bash denies below are therefore defense-in-depth, not a boundary.
